# OlogGuy7 — combat guide

- Original source: [OlogGuy7 — combat guide](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2930272620)
- Author / publication: OlogGuy7 / Steam Community
- Language / date: English; published 2023-02-08; updated 2024-04-25
- Access: Full guide page retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: none found in the Wayback Machine (checked 2026-09-09)
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (no redistribution grant on Steam guides, so not transcribed)

Explains mouse gestures and practical nonlethal fighting. Straight strokes produce thrusts or directional strikes; wider arcs cover more space; a circle attacks surrounding enemies; an infinity-shaped gesture produces a slow power attack. Right-click is described as blocking.

The author emphasizes spacing, interrupting opponents, prioritizing archers, and combining combat with nets or wasps. Will Scarlet, Little John, Friar Tuck, and the club-wielding generic recruit receive distinct tactical roles. The club recruit is praised for drawing and attacking quickly.

The guide warns about friendly hits, vulnerable recovery animations, fighting uphill on stairs, and leaving unconscious enemies where patrols can find them. Binding and carrying bodies are part of the combat plan. Quick Actions can coordinate an engagement, but long action sequences are described as less reliable.

**Limitations:** effectiveness rankings and timing advice are player experience; verify gesture recognition and damage behavior separately.

## Detailed notes

Guide metadata at retrieval: posted 8 Feb 2023 6:32am, updated 25 Apr 2024 3:55pm; categories Gameplay Basics, Walkthroughs; 610 unique visitors, 12 favourites, 5 comments, "Not enough ratings". Sections: When to Fight, The Combat Gestures, Positioning and Planning, Who (and When) to Use, Things to Watch Out For, Specific Takedowns/Combinations, Conclusions. Steam guides carry no redistribution grant, so the prose is not transcribed.

**When to fight.** The author argues this is not a game where breaking stealth is always worst: some stages make stealth takedowns with Robin or Little John infeasible, and the game sometimes detects the player before the takedown completes, especially on Hard.

**Gesture table** (as described by the author):

| Mouse gesture | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Straight line up | Lunge; with club or quarterstaff almost always a temporary knockdown |
| Straight line left or right | Fairly quick bash from that side |
| Click on enemy, or straight line down | Very quick tap; small damage, interrupts the enemy's attack |
| Right-click | Blocks most incoming attacks |
| Semicircle left or right | Same as side slash with larger hit area and slower timing |
| Full circle | Hits everyone around the character; somewhat slow, misses a small arc; crowd control |
| Infinity sign | Power attack; long charge, very high damage with every weapon |

**Positioning.** Assess the target first (a lone archer versus three knights); combine attacks with Stutely's net or Friar Tuck's wasp nest before charging; use alleys so side bashes hit several enemies, or a full circle in the middle of a crowd; keep distance to avoid being rushed; kill archers first because they stun-lock; use a second character as a distraction; Robin or Little John can one-punch an enemy already engaged with someone else.

**Character ranking** (author's lightning-bolt ratings): Club henchman 3, Will Scarlet 2, Little John 2, Friar Tuck 1, Stutely 1, archer henchman and fork henchman unrated. Will: fast flail strikes, best against knights, spamming side bashes "virtually never fails", shield distracts archers if he faces them. Little John: slow to deploy, huge range, knocks out before enemies close, very vulnerable to arrows, slow swings so side bashes have diminishing returns. Club henchman: fastest weapon draw, works like either Will or John, good even with few combat stars, can jab to interrupt late-game enemies who otherwise sneak in a hit. Tuck: mace good for single targets, do not overextend. Stutely: bait and parry at full combat stars. Archer henchman: shield up to soak archer fire, can reach odd places by climbing. Fork henchman: side bashes knock out weaker enemies; use to let better men train.

**Warnings.** Friendly fire from area attacks or fighting shoulder to shoulder; retreat and hide when losing, enemies give up the search after a while (also a way to bait traps); fight from the top of stairs, never from the bottom; hide knocked-out enemies because guards search everywhere once a post is empty, with Stutely or the archer tying and John or the club henchman carrying; fallen enemies knock over neighbours like dominoes; a patrol expects to see the sentry it halts beside, so sometimes sneaking past is better.

**Combinations.** Basic takedown: approach from behind, click to engage, spam side bashes. Crowd control: full circle in the middle, then wide semicircles; add Stutely's net (timing must match or the net is removed at once) or Tuck's wasps (cannot be removed). Armoured units (knights, black guards) block better: alternate side bashes with forward lunges until they are down, then finish with a power attack. Quick actions: square map icon bottom right, assign, press space to trigger.

**Comments.** The author (8 Sep 2024) says long quick-action queues raise the chance of a failure, knockouts can fail so keep a backup, and ordering can be controlled by positioning characters at different distances since actions like Stutely's net take time. A reader reports Little John trains melee best in their experience and asks whether only Robin trains archers; another asks how to loot bodies.

When to Fight 

This is not a traditional stealth game where breaking stealth is always the poorest option. There are several stages where stealth take-downs with Robin/Little John is not feasible. Moreover, this game will sometimes unfairly 'detect' the player before they can complete the take-down action, especially on Hard difficulty. So, you will quite frequently have to get an enemy down in combat rather than stealth.  
  


The Combat Gestures 

There are quite a few different gestures you draw with your cursor that initiate different attacks. They are listed below:  
  


  * Straight line up **↥** \- Lunge towards the enemy. With the blunt weapons such as the club/quarterstaff, this almost always results in a temporary knockdown for the enemy.  
  

  * Right/Left Side Slash '**←/⟶** ' - A fairly quick bash from the direction you draw the straight line.   
  

  * Click on Enemy '**🡤** ' or straight line down **↓** \- Very quick tap on the enemy. Useful to get a quick bit of damage or interrupt their attack.  
  

  * Right Click - Block most of incoming attacks.  
  

  * Semi-Circle Left/Right '**(** / **)** ' - Same as the side slash above but with a larger hit space with a slower attack time.  
  

  * Full-Circle '**⟲** ' - Hit everyone in a circle around you. Somewhat slow and misses a small section of the circle but good for crowd control.   
  

  * Infinity Sign '**∞** ' - Power attack. Takes a while to charge up but hits like a truck with all weapons.



Positioning and Planning 

  * First, _assess the enemy/enemies you're about to attack_. 🦉  
Charging a lone archer is easy. Charging 3 knights is more difficult. In the case of the latter, it's a good idea to combine your attack with another character. For example, just before charging, use Stutely's net to trap some of the enemies or Friar Tuck's wasp nest to stagger them. Combat should only be done when stealth fails.  
  

  * Second, _plan your fighting moves in advance_. 🎯  
If you're going into a crowd of people, then trying to cram your enemy into an alley way and spam left/right bash (which hits multiple people) will be effective. Otherwise, running into a crowd of enemies and using full circle bash will work to give you some breathing room or set-up another character to attack. Regardless, use the environment to your advantage.  
  

  * Third, _be mindful of your positioning_. 🚩  
Maintain a good fighting distance so you can't be crowd rushed. Fighting whilst 2 enemy archers are using you as a pincushion is not fun. Go for the archers first as they can stun-lock your men. You send another one of your men to distract some of the enemies while you engage the high threat targets (archers, officers, etc). Also remember that Robin/Little John can 1 hit KO punch an enemy in combat if said enemy is already engaged in combat with someone else.



Who (and When) to Use 

There are only a few characters in this game who can reliably fight without taking too much damage and without killing the enemy. This guide is tailored towards the non-lethal armed characters as this is the best way to get merry-men and keep your conscience clear!   
  


  * ⚡⚡ **Will Scarlet** \- Quick and fast flail strikes on a single target, especially useful against the tougher Knights. Spamming left and right bashes virtually never fails. Shield is useful to distract archers so long as he faces them.   
  

  * ⚡⚡ **Little John** \- Takes a while to deploy but has a huge range and can knock out enemies without them getting close. Very vulnerable to archer fire. Left/right bashes often have diminishing returns as his swing speed is quite slow, so make every hit count.   
  

  * ⚡⚡⚡ **Club Henchman** \- Can be used like Will Scarlet's flail or like Little John's quarterstaff. Deploys his club very quickly and is versatile. Can perform quick take-downs on a single target and also has good crowd control. Very vulnerable to archer fire.  
  

  * ⚡ **Friar Tuck** \- His mace is good for single target combat and can reliably knockout targets like Will Scarlet but don't let him get over-extended. Very vulnerable to archer fire.  
  

  * ⚡ **Stutely** \- To bait and distract the enemies. At full combat stars he can parry quite well and can hold some enemies off while Robin/Little John knock them out or one of your other guys engage them. Technically, anyone can do Stutely's role but I found it to be more successful using him than anyone else.   
  

  * **Archer Henchman** \- There are a few instances where pulling out your shield and suppressing archer fire is useful as bait. Works well as a distraction, especially using the henchman's ability to parkour and get to unusual places and make it hard for melee units to engage.   
  

  * **Fork Henchman** \- Can take on weaker enemies with left/right bashes to knock them out. He is more liable to get damaged but can be used in a pinch when the above aren't around. Use when you want to let your other men train in Sherwood

  
You may be wondering why I ranked the Club Henchman above the rest and this is mainly because of _a)_ he has the quickest weapon draw speed and _b)_ he is very useful even with few combat stars.   
  
In the later missions of the game, enemies attack much faster and even if you're the one who initiates combat, the enemy can manage to sneak in a quick attack. With virtually all other characters, this means they will take damage, but the Club Henchman can perform a quick jab attack to interrupt and come out unscathed. Being separated from your healers or having to persistently enter combat is common - saving your health is important. 

Things to Watch Out For 

  * You can hit your own men if they attack while they are fighting close to each other or if you do an area attack (e.g full circle swing) with one of your guys within its radius. Make sure your fighters have room to breathe.  
  

  * If you're losing a fight but you've achieved something significant (e.g you've taken out an officer or you've achieved a sub-objective) there's no need to continue - just run away and hide somewhere. You can always come back if necessary. Once you have left the enemy line of sight, after a while they should give up the search. This is a good way to lure the enemy into traps or ambushes too.  
  

  * Stairs are good places to fight when you're on top of them, they are bad places to fight when you are at the bottom. Unless you want to become a human snowball, never try to fight an enemy located at the top of a staircase.  
  

  * Hide your knocked out enemies. This seems obvious but the enemy can and will search every nook and cranny in the map for even noticing that a guard is not at their post. Have Stutely or an Archer Henchman nearby and ready to tie people up as soon as the fighting stops. Likewise have Little John or the Club Henchman ready to carry the tied enemies away.   
  

  * People are like dominos. If they are in a dense area, one person will fall onto another and so on. You can use this to even the odds in a fight and keep focused on one target at a time.   
  

  * Decide whether it's worth taking out an enemy or just sneaking by. A patrol that halts near a sentry will expect to see him there each time. Sometimes it's not worth risking HP or alerting the entire garrison just because an opportunity for a take-down is forthcoming.



Specific Takedowns/Combinations 

Below is a list of specific combinations that I've used, though there may be others I haven't considered. It's assumed that you know how to plan quick actions (Click the square map icon in the bottom right and assign an action. Pressing space will initiate the planned action).   
  


  * ⚜️⚜️⚜️ Basic Takedown (Anybody) - Make sure enemy is relatively isolated and won't alert any other guards when they detect you. Walk up to them from behind and click on them to initiate combat. Spam left/right bash until they get KO'd.   
  

  * ⚜️ Basic Crowd Control (Little John/Club Henchman) - Navigate yourself into the middle of a crowd of enemies and use the full circle swing. Continue doing this until there are manageable amount of soldiers and use wide semi-circle swings if you aren't completely surrounded.   
  
\+ ⚜️ (Stutely) - Use Stutely's net to capture a few of the soldiers whilst quickly running in your fighter to engage the rest. Make sure to synchronize the timing of the attacks otherwise the net will be immediately removed.   
  
\+ ⚜️ (Friar Tuck) - Use wasps nest to stagger the enemies whilst quickly running in your fighter to engage the rest. This is similar to Stutely's attack but the wasps effect cannot be removed.   
  

  * ⚜️⚜️Armored Unit Takedown (Blunt Weapon Users) - Knights and Blackguard soldiers know how to block better than the lower tier soldiers, so switch up your moves. Side bashes should be used with forward lunges until the enemy is on the ground. If timed right, a power attack can be used to finish them off. 



Conclusions 

I would appreciate any feedback about this guide! I really enjoyed this game and the combat system was definitely one of the reasons why.

I'm not sure if it's the fact of a character being unique or if it's because they have a high melee/archery skill that allows them to train recruits better, I'll need to test that as I rarely usef archery.  
  
Quick actions can be useful but I found that the more actions you add to the queue, the greater the chance that one of your characters will screw up. Keep it limited and maximize your prob of success - e.g when using Will Scarlett's slingshot make sure he has a clear line of sight. Some actions (like knockouts with Robin or Little John) can fail so make sure to have a backup plan. I also found it useful to kite the enemies into more favorable positions.   
  
Otherwise, the key is timing. Be aware of the time it takes to perform the actions - e.g Stutely takes some time to fish out the net and throw it. If you want the actions to happen in a particular order, you can delay some characters by positioning them further away.
